Incorporating Beige Book insights alongside the SLOOS and the January 26, 2022 FOMC statement slightly tempers the earlier uplift. District reports indicate modest-to-moderate growth overall, with Omicron weighing on leisure and hospitality and dampening retail foot traffic in the near term. Manufacturing, freight, and business services remained solid; labor markets were very tight with strong wage gains, and price pressures were broad-based amid ongoing supply constraints. Banks generally saw firmer C&I loan demand and some easing in standards, but household credit demand—especially for residential real estate—softened as mortgage rates rose.

Net effect: The Beige Book corroborates solid business activity and labor gains but highlights near-term consumer and services headwinds from Omicron and persistent inflation/supply frictions. Relative to the SLOOS-driven +0.10, the Beige Book nudges the balance slightly lower but still mildly positive.
